sentences.zh: 隱逸中

translations.literal: Recluses, Part Two (Middle Section)
translations.idiomatic: Recluses (Part Two)

sentences.zh: ○王樵張愈黃晞周啟明代淵陳烈孫侔劉易薑潛連庶章詧俞汝尚陽孝本鄧考甫宇文之邵吳瑛鬆江漁翁杜生順昌山人南安翁張舉

translations.literal: Wang Qiao, Zhang Yu, Huang Xi, Zhou Qiming, Dai Yuan, Chen Lie, Sun Mou, Liu Yi, Jiang Qian, Lian Shu, Zhang Cha, Yu Rushang, Yang Xiaoben, Deng Kaofu, Yuwen Zhishao, Wu Ying, Songjiang Fisherman, Du Sheng, Shunchang Mountain Man, Nan'an Old Man, Zhang Ju
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao, Zhang Yu, Huang Xi, Zhou Qiming, Dai Yuan, Chen Lie, Sun Mou, Liu Yi, Jiang Qian, Lian Shu, Zhang Cha, Yu Rushang, Yang Xiaoben, Deng Kaofu, Yuwen Zhishao, Wu Ying, the Songjiang Fisherman, Du Sheng, the Shunchang Mountain Man, the Nan'an Old Man, and Zhang Ju

sentences.zh: 王樵，字肩望，淄州淄川人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiao, style name Jianwang, was a native of Zichuan in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao, whose style was Jianwang, came from Zichuan in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 居縣北梓桐山。

translations.literal: He lived on Zitong Mountain north of the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: He made his home on Zitong Mountain, north of the county.

sentences.zh: 博通群書，不治章句，尤善考《易》。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered many books, did not pursue exegetical commentary, and was especially skilled in investigating the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely across the classics but did not trouble himself with philological glosses, and was especially adept at studying the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 與賈同、李冠齊名，學者多從之。

translations.literal: He was equally famous with Jia Tong and Li Guan, and many students followed him.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation stood alongside Jia Tong's and Li Guan's, and a great many scholars sought him out as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，契丹遊騎度河，舉家被掠。

translations.literal: During the Xianping era, Khitan scouting horsemen crossed the river, and his entire household was carried off.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianping period, Khitan raiders crossed the river and seized his whole family.

sentences.zh: 樵即棄妻，挺身入契丹訪父母，累年不獲，還東山。

translations.literal: Qiao immediately abandoned his wife, went alone into Khitan territory to seek his parents, failed to find them after many years, and returned to Eastern Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao at once left his wife behind and went alone into Khitan lands in search of his parents. After years without success, he returned to his home on the eastern mountain.

sentences.zh: 刻木招魂以葬，立祠畫像，事之如生，服喪六年，哀動行路。

translations.literal: He carved wooden spirit tablets to summon the souls for burial, erected a shrine with portraits, served them as if alive, observed mourning for six years, and his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He carved wooden spirit tablets for a soul-summoning burial, built a shrine with painted portraits, and tended them as though his parents were still alive. He wore mourning for six years, and his grief moved all who passed along the road.

sentences.zh: 又為屬之尊者次第成服，北望歎曰：「身世如此，自比於人可乎！

translations.literal: He also completed the graded mourning garments for affiliated elders in sequence, looked north and sighed, saying: "My body and fate are like this—can I compare myself with other men!"
translations.idiomatic: He also arranged the proper graduated mourning for elder relatives under his care. Gazing northward, he sighed and said, "Given what my life and fate have become, how can I measure myself against ordinary men?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與俗絕，自稱贅世翁，唯以論兵擊劍為事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he cut himself off from common society, called himself Master Surplus-World, and took discussion of warfare and swordplay as his sole occupation.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he broke with the world, styled himself the Surplus-World Elder, and devoted himself solely to military strategy and swordsmanship.

sentences.zh: 一驢負裝，徒步千里，晚年屢遊塞下。

translations.literal: One donkey bore his baggage; he traveled a thousand li on foot; in his later years he often roamed the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: A single donkey carried his pack as he walked a thousand li on foot; in his old age he traveled the northern borderlands repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 畫策幹何承矩、耿望，求滅遼復仇，不用。

translations.literal: He drafted plans and presented them to He Chengzu and Geng Wang, seeking to destroy Liao and take revenge; they were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He presented stratagems to He Chengzu and Geng Wang, urging the destruction of Liao to avenge his family, but his proposals were rejected.

sentences.zh: 乃於城東南隅累磚自環，謂之「繭室」。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the southeast corner of the city he piled bricks to enclose himself and called it the "Cocoon Chamber."
translations.idiomatic: He then built a circular enclosure of stacked bricks at the city's southeast corner and called it the Cocoon Chamber.

sentences.zh: 銘其門曰：「天生王樵，薄命寡智，材不濟時，道號『贅世』。

translations.literal: He inscribed his gate, saying: "Heaven engendered Wang Qiao—thin fate, scant wisdom, talent not suited to the age, the Way-title 'Surplus-World.'"
translations.idiomatic: He inscribed his doorway: "Heaven gave birth to Wang Qiao—ill-fated, little wit, talents ill-suited to the times, his Way-name 'Surplus-World.'"

sentences.zh: 生而為室，以備不虞，死則藏形，不虞乃備。

translations.literal: Living, it serves as a chamber against the unforeseen; dying, it conceals the form—against the unforeseen one is prepared.
translations.idiomatic: "In life it is my dwelling against the unforeseen; in death it will conceal my body. Thus am I prepared for every contingency."

sentences.zh: 」病革，入室自掩戶卒。

translations.literal: " When his illness became critical, he entered the chamber, closed the door himself, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " When his illness turned critical, he entered the chamber, shut the door from within, and died.

sentences.zh: 治平末，職方郎中向宗道知淄州，訪繭室，已構屋為民居。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhiping era, Xiang Zongdao of the Bureau of Appointments served as prefect of Zizhou; he visited the Cocoon Chamber, which had already been built over as dwellings for residents.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhiping reign, Xiang Zongdao of the Bureau of Military Appointments became prefect of Zizhou. When he visited the Cocoon Chamber, houses for ordinary residents had already been built on the site.

sentences.zh: 得樵甥牟氏子，乃知改葬。

translations.literal: He obtained Qiao's nephew, a son of the Mou clan, and only then learned of the reburial.
translations.idiomatic: Through Qiao's nephew, a Mou-clan youth, he learned that the remains had been reinterred elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 因而即其地復作繭室及祠堂，刻石以記之。

translations.literal: Accordingly, on that site he rebuilt the Cocoon Chamber and ancestral shrine and carved stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore rebuilt the Cocoon Chamber and memorial shrine on the original spot and set up a stone inscription to commemorate Qiao.

sentences.zh: 張愈字少愚，益州郫人，其先自河東徙。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu, style name Shao'en, was a native of Pi in Yizhou; his ancestors had moved from Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, styled Shao'en, came from Pi in Yizhou; his family had originally migrated from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 愈雋偉有大志，遊學四方，屢舉不第。

translations.literal: Yu was handsome and imposing with great ambitions; he traveled to study in all directions and repeatedly failed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was tall and striking, with lofty ambitions. He traveled widely to study, yet repeatedly failed the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 寶元初，上書言邊事，請使契丹，令外夷相攻，以完中國之勢，其論甚壯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoyuan era, he submitted a memorial on frontier affairs, requesting to be sent to Khitan so that outer barbarians might attack one another and thereby complete the power of China; his argument was very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoyuan reign, he memorialized the throne on border policy, proposing that he be sent to Khitan to set the outer tribes fighting one another and thereby secure the Central States. His argument was bold and compelling.

sentences.zh: 用使者薦，除試秘書省校書郎，願以授父顯忠而隱於家。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of an envoy, he was appointed provisional collator of the Secretariat; he wished to confer it on his father Xianzhong and himself remain in seclusion at home.
translations.idiomatic: On an envoy's recommendation he was appointed provisional collator in the Secretariat, but he asked that the post be given to his father Xianzhong instead while he himself remained in retirement at home.

sentences.zh: 文彥博治蜀，為置青城山白雲溪杜光庭故居以處之。

translations.literal: When Wen Yanbo governed Shu, he set up for him the former residence of Du Guangting at Baiyun Stream on Mount Qingcheng as his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo governed Shu, he arranged for Yu to live in Du Guangting's former home at Baiyun Stream on Mount Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，鹽酪不入口。

translations.literal: When he suffered the death of his mother within the gates, he did not let salt or dairy enter his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his mother's death he took no salt or dairy whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 再期，植所持柳杖於墓，忽生枝葉，後合抱。

translations.literal: At the end of the second mourning period, he planted the willow staff he had carried at the grave; it suddenly sprouted branches and leaves, and later grew to a trunk one could embrace.
translations.idiomatic: When the second mourning period ended, he planted the willow staff he had carried at his mother's grave. It suddenly put forth branches and leaves and eventually grew thick enough to encircle with one's arms.

sentences.zh: 六召不應。

translations.literal: Six summonses—he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned six times and never answered.

sentences.zh: 喜奕棋。

translations.literal: He delighted in playing weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of chess.

sentences.zh: 樂山水，遇有興，雖數千里輒盡室往。

translations.literal: He delighted in mountains and waters; when the mood struck him, even if several thousand li distant, he would take his whole household and go.
translations.idiomatic: He loved mountains and rivers, and whenever the spirit moved him he would take his entire household on journeys of thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 遂浮湘、沅，觀浙江，升羅浮，入九疑，買石載鶴以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he floated on the Xiang and Yuan, viewed the Zhe River, ascended Mount Luofu, entered Mount Jiuyi, bought stones and carried cranes home.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled the Xiang and Yuan by boat, visited the Zhe River, climbed Mount Luofu, entered Mount Jiuyi, and returned home laden with ornamental stones and cranes.

sentences.zh: 杜門著書，未就，卒。

translations.literal: He shut his doors to write books; before completion, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself in to write, but died before his work was finished.

sentences.zh: 妻蒲氏名芝，賢而有文，為之誄曰：「高視往古，哲士實殷，施及秦、漢，餘烈氛氳。

translations.literal: His wife, of the Pu clan, named Zhi, was worthy and literary; she composed his dirge, saying: "Looking high upon antiquity, wise men were truly numerous; their influence reached through Qin and Han, their lingering glory thick as mist."
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Pu, whose given name was Zhi, was virtuous and accomplished in letters. She composed his dirge, which begins: "Gazing back upon antiquity, one sees that wise men were plentiful indeed; their influence extended through Qin and Han, and their lingering glory still hangs in the air."

sentences.zh: 挺生英傑，卓爾逸群，孰謂今世，亦有其人。

translations.literal: " A towering hero was born, outstanding beyond the crowd—who would say that in the present age there is also such a man?"
translations.idiomatic: "A towering hero arose, surpassing all his peers—who would have thought that our own age, too, could produce such a man?"

sentences.zh: 其人伊何？

translations.literal: " Who is this man?"
translations.idiomatic: "And who was this man?"

sentences.zh: 白雲隱君。

translations.literal: " The White Cloud Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: "The Recluse of White Cloud Stream."

sentences.zh: 嘗曰丈夫，趨世不偶，仕非其志，祿不可苟，營營末途，非吾所守。

translations.literal: " He once said: A true man, rushing with the age yet not finding his match—office is not his will, emolument cannot be sought casually; bustling along the lower path is not what I uphold."
translations.idiomatic: "He once said: A true man may press forward in the world yet never find his proper place. Office was not his desire, and salary was not to be grasped at casually. The scramble for petty advancement was not the path he chose to follow."

sentences.zh: 吾生有涯，少實多艱，窮亦自固，困亦不顛。

translations.literal: " My life has its bounds; in youth much hardship, in poverty I still hold firm, in distress I do not topple."
translations.idiomatic: "My life has its limits; youth brought more hardship than ease. In poverty he held firm, and in adversity he did not fall."

sentences.zh: 不貴人爵，知命樂天，脫簪散發，眠雲聽泉。

translations.literal: " He did not prize human ranks; knowing fate, he rejoiced in Heaven; he removed his hairpin and let his hair fall loose, sleeping among clouds and listening to springs."
translations.idiomatic: "He did not prize human rank; knowing his fate, he took joy in Heaven's decree. He cast aside his hairpin and let his hair flow free, sleeping among the clouds and listening to mountain springs."

sentences.zh: 有峰千仞，有溪數曲，廣成遺趾，吳興高躅。

translations.literal: " There were peaks a thousand ren high, streams winding in several bends, traces left by Guangcheng, lofty footsteps of Wu Xing."
translations.idiomatic: "There were peaks a thousand ren high and streams winding in many bends—the footprints of Guangchengzi, the lofty traces of the sages of Wu."

sentences.zh: 疏石通逕，依林架屋，麋鹿同群，晝遊夜息。

translations.literal: " He cleared stones to open paths, built dwellings leaning on the forest, roamed with deer as one flock, active by day and resting by night."
translations.idiomatic: "He cleared stones to lay paths, built his dwelling against the forest, and ranged with deer as his companions—wandering by day and resting by night."

sentences.zh: 嶺月破雲，秋霖灑竹，清意何窮，真心自得，放言遺慮，何榮何辱？

translations.literal: " Ridge-moon breaking through clouds, autumn rains sprinkling bamboo—pure intent without end, true heart self-attained; letting words go and leaving cares behind—what glory, what disgrace?"
translations.idiomatic: "Moonlight on the ridge breaking through clouds, autumn rain sprinkling the bamboo—his pure intent knew no end, his true heart found its own fulfillment. He spoke freely and cast cares aside: what glory, what disgrace?"

sentences.zh: 孟春感疾，閉戶不出，豈期遂往，英標永隔。

translations.literal: " In early spring he felt illness, shut his door and did not go out—who expected he would depart so soon, his heroic mark forever parted."
translations.idiomatic: "In early spring illness seized him; he shut his door and did not emerge. Who could have foreseen that he would depart so soon, his noble spirit parted from us forever?"

sentences.zh: 抒詞哽噎，揮涕汍瀾，人誰無死，惜乎材賢。

translations.literal: " Expressing words with choked voice, waving tears in overflowing streams—who among men does not die? Alas for such talent and worth."
translations.idiomatic: "My words choke in my throat, my tears fall in torrents—all men must die, yet how grievous to lose such talent and virtue."

sentences.zh: 已矣吾人，嗚呼哀哉！」

translations.literal: " He is gone, our man—alas, how mournful!""
translations.idiomatic: "He is gone, our beloved—alas, how mournful!""

sentences.zh: 黃晞，字景微，建安人。

translations.literal: Huang Xi, style name Jingwei, was a native of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xi, whose style was Jingwei, came from Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 少通經，聚書數千卷，學者多從之遊，自號聱隅子。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered the classics, gathered several thousand scrolls of books, and many students followed him in study; he styled himself Master Obscure Corner.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he mastered the classics and amassed several thousand volumes. Many students came to study with him, and he styled himself the Obscure Corner Master.

sentences.zh: 著《歔欷瑣微論》十卷，以謂聱隅者枿物之名，歔欷者歎聲，瑣微者述辭也。

translations.literal: He authored the Ten Scrolls of Sighs and Trifling Subtleties, explaining that 'obscure corner' is the name of a sprouting plant, 'sighs' are sounds of lamentation, and 'trifling subtleties' are words of exposition.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the ten-scroll Treatise on Sighs and Trifling Subtleties, explaining that 'obscure corner' names a sprouting plant, 'sighs' denotes lamentation, and 'trifling subtleties' refers to his mode of discourse.

sentences.zh: 石介在太學，遣諸生以禮聘召，晞走匿鄰家不出。

translations.literal: When Shi Jie was at the Imperial Academy, he sent students with ritual gifts to summon him; Xi fled and hid at a neighbor's home and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jie was director of the Imperial Academy, he sent students with formal gifts to invite Xi to serve. Xi fled and hid at a neighbor's house, refusing to emerge.

sentences.zh: 樞密使韓琦表薦之，以為太學助教致仕。

translations.literal: Privy Councillor Han Qi memorialized recommending him and appointed him Assistant Instructor at the Imperial Academy with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Councillor Han Qi recommended him by memorial, and he was appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy with permission to retire from active duty.

sentences.zh: 受命一夕卒。

translations.literal: The night he received the appointment, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the very night he accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 代淵，字蘊之，本代州人。

translations.literal: Dai Yuan, style name Yunzhi, was originally a native of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yuan, whose style was Yunzhi, was originally from Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 唐末，避地導江，家世為吏，有陰德。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, the family fled to Daojiang; for generations they had been officials and possessed hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tang dynasty the family fled to Daojiang. For generations they had served as officials, and their line had accumulated hidden merit.

sentences.zh: 淵性簡潔，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was simple and unadorned; in serving his parents he was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was plain and unassuming in character, and was renowned for his filial devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 受學於李畋、張達。

translations.literal: He received learning from Li Tian and Zhang Da.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Li Tian and Zhang Da.

sentences.zh: 年四十，鄉人更勸，舉進士甲科，得清水主簿。

translations.literal: At age forty, fellow townsmen urged him again; he passed the jinshi examination in the top class and obtained the post of registrar of Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: At forty, his fellow townsmen urged him once more. He passed the jinshi examination in the top class and was appointed registrar of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「祿不及親，何所為耶？

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "The salary did not reach my parents—what was it all for?"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "This salary came too late for my parents—what was the point of it all?"

sentences.zh: 」還家教授，坐席常滿。

translations.literal: " He returned home to teach; his seats were always full.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned home to teach, and his lecture hall was always full.

sentences.zh: 安撫使舉鳳州團練推官，不就。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner recommended him as militia training push-official of Fengzhou; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner recommended him for the post of militia training push-official in Feng Prefecture, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 知益州楊日嚴又薦之，遂以太子中允致仕。

translations.literal: Yang Riyan, prefect of Yizhou, recommended him again, and he was granted retirement as Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Riyan, prefect of Yizhou, recommended him again, and he was granted retirement with the title of vice director in the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 謝絕諸生，著《周易旨要》、《老佛雜說》數十篇。

translations.literal: He declined all students and authored several tens of scrolls including Essentials of the Book of Changes and Miscellaneous Discourses on Laozi and Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: He declined further students and wrote several dozen works, including Essentials of the Book of Changes and Miscellaneous Discourses on Laozi and Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 田況上其書，自太常丞改祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Tian Kuang presented his books to the throne; he was changed from Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices to Outer Gentleman of the Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Kuang presented his writings to the throne, and Yuan was promoted from vice director of the Imperial Sacrifices to outer gentleman of the Ancestral Temples.

sentences.zh: 晚年日菜食，巾褐山水間，自號虛一子。

translations.literal: In his later years he ate vegetables daily, wore cloth headwrap and brown robe among mountains and waters, and styled himself Master Void-One.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he ate only vegetables, dressed in plain cloth and brown robes among the mountains and streams, and styled himself the Void-One Master.

sentences.zh: 長吏歲時致問，澹然與對，略不及私。

translations.literal: Senior officials sent seasonal inquiries; he responded calmly, scarcely touching on private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials sent seasonal greetings; he responded calmly and scarcely mentioned private affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年九月，有疾，召術士擇日，雲「丙申吉」，頷之，是日沐浴而絕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Jiayou, he fell ill, summoned a diviner to choose a day, who said "bingchen is auspicious"; he nodded assent, and on that day bathed and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Jiayou he fell ill. He summoned a diviner to choose an auspicious day; told that the day bingchen was favorable, he nodded assent, bathed on that day, and died.

sentences.zh: 陳烈字季慈，福州候官人。

translations.literal: Chen Lie, style name Jici, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lie, whose style was Jici, came from Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 性介僻，篤於孝友。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and aloof; he was devoted to filial piety and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and reserved by nature, and devoted to filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，勺飲不入於口五日，自壯及老，奉事如生。

translations.literal: During mourning for his parents, for five days not a spoonful of drink entered his mouth; from his prime to his old age, he served them as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his parents he took not a spoonful of food or drink for five days. From his prime through old age he served them as though they were still alive.

sentences.zh: 學行端飭，動遵古禮，平居終日不言，禦童仆如對賓客。

translations.literal: His learning and conduct were proper and restrained; in movement he followed ancient ritual; in ordinary life he did not speak all day; he treated servants and pages as if facing guests.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship and conduct were rigorous and proper; he followed ancient ritual in all his actions. In daily life he might go an entire day without speaking, and he treated servants and pages with the courtesy due to guests.

sentences.zh: 里中人敬之，冠昏喪祭，請而後行。

translations.literal: People of his village revered him; for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, they invited him before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors held him in deep respect; for capping ceremonies, weddings, funerals, and sacrifices they would invite him before proceeding.

sentences.zh: 從學者常數百。

translations.literal: Students who followed him often numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly had several hundred students.

sentences.zh: 賢父兄訓子弟，必舉烈言行以示之。

translations.literal: Worthy fathers and elder brothers instructing sons and younger brothers would invariably cite Lie's words and conduct to show them.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous fathers and elder brothers instructing their sons and younger brothers invariably cited Lie's words and conduct as examples.

sentences.zh: 嘗以鄉薦試京師不利，即罷舉。

translations.literal: Once recommended by his district, he tried the examinations in the capital without success and thereupon ceased competing.
translations.idiomatic: Having been recommended by his district, he tried the metropolitan examinations without success and thereafter gave up competing.

sentences.zh: 或勉之求仕，則曰：「伊尹守道，成湯三聘以幣；

translations.literal: When some urged him to seek office, he said: "Yi Yin upheld the Way, and Cheng Tang thrice invited him with gifts;"
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to seek office, he said, "Yi Yin upheld the Way, and King Cheng of Shang invited him three times with gifts."

sentences.zh: 呂望既老，文王載之俱歸。

translations.literal: " Lü Wang was already old, yet King Wen carried him home together."
translations.idiomatic: "Lü Wang was already old when King Wen of Zhou brought him home in his own carriage."

sentences.zh: 今天子仁聖好賢，有湯、文之心，豈無先覺如伊、呂者乎？

translations.literal: " Today's Son of Heaven is benevolent and sage, loving worthies, possessing the hearts of Tang and Wen—how could there fail to be foreknowing men like Yi and Lü?"
translations.idiomatic: "Our present emperor is benevolent and sage, and loves worthy men—he has the hearts of Tang and Wen. Surely there must be foreknowing sages like Yi Yin and Lü Wang among us?"

sentences.zh: 」仁宗屢詔之，不起。

translations.literal: " Emperor Renzong repeatedly summoned him, but he did not rise to office.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Renzong summoned him repeatedly, but he never accepted office.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，應曰：「吾學未成也。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, he replied: "My learning is not yet complete."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he replied, "My learning is not yet complete."

sentences.zh: 」公卿大夫、郡守、鄉老交章稱其賢。

translations.literal: " High ministers, grandees, prefects, and village elders submitted successive memorials praising his worth.
translations.idiomatic: " Ministers, grandees, prefects, and village elders submitted successive memorials praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，以為本州教授，歐陽修又言之，召為國子直講，皆不拜。

translations.literal: During Jiayou, he was made professor of his home prefecture; Ouyang Xiu spoke for him again, and he was summoned as Direct Lecturer of the Imperial Academy—all without accepting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou reign he was appointed professor in his home prefecture. Ouyang Xiu spoke on his behalf again, and he was summoned as direct lecturer at the Imperial Academy—but he accepted none of these appointments.

sentences.zh: 已而福建提刑王陶言其為妻林氏所訟，因詆烈貪詐，乞奪所受恩。

translations.literal: Later Wang Tao, Fujian judicial commissioner, reported that he had been sued by his wife Lady Lin, and on that basis slandered Lie as greedy and deceitful, requesting revocation of the favors he had received.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Tao, judicial commissioner of Fujian, reported that Lie had been sued by his wife, Lady Lin, and on that basis denounced him as greedy and deceitful, asking that the honors he had received be revoked.

sentences.zh: 司馬光為諫官，率同列爭曰：「臣等每患士無名檢，故舉烈以厲風俗。

translations.literal: Sima Guang as remonstrance official led his colleagues in disputing, saying: "We ministers are always troubled that scholars lack moral restraint, and therefore recommended Lie to encourage custom."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, serving as a remonstrance official, led his colleagues in protest, saying, "We are constantly troubled that scholars lack moral restraint, and for that reason we recommended Lie to encourage proper conduct."

sentences.zh: 烈平生操守，出於誠實，雖有迂闊不合中道，猶為守節之士，當保而全之。

translations.literal: " Lie's lifelong conduct sprang from sincerity; though somewhat rigid and not fully conforming to the mean way, he is still a man who upholds integrity and should be protected and preserved whole."
translations.idiomatic: "Lie has conducted himself with sincerity throughout his life. Though he may be somewhat rigid and not always conform to the golden mean, he remains a man of integrity who should be protected and preserved."

sentences.zh: 若夫婦不相諧，則聽之離絕，毋使節行之士為橫辱所挫。

translations.literal: " If husband and wife are not in harmony, then let them be permitted to separate—do not let a man of integrity be broken by wanton insult."
translations.idiomatic: "If husband and wife cannot live in harmony, let them be permitted to separate—but do not let a man of integrity be crushed by base slander."

sentences.zh: 」陶說遂不行。

translations.literal: " Tao's proposal thereupon was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Tao's proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，部使者申薦之，詔從其尚，以宣德郎致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, the regional envoy recommended him; an edict followed his preference, and he was granted retirement as Gentleman for Extending Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou reign the regional commissioner recommended him; the court honored his wishes and granted him retirement with the rank of gentleman for extending virtue.

sentences.zh: 明年，復教授本州。

translations.literal: The following year, he was again made professor of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again appointed professor in his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在職不受廩奉，鄉里問遺絲毫無所受；

translations.literal: While in office he did not accept salary; from village and neighborhood he accepted not the slightest gift;
translations.idiomatic: While in office he accepted no salary, and refused every gift offered by neighbors and townsfolk;

sentences.zh: 家租有餘，則推以濟貧乏。

translations.literal: when household rents had surplus, he distributed them to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: when his household income exceeded his needs, he gave the surplus to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 孫侔，字少述，與王安石、曾鞏遊，名傾一時。

translations.literal: Sun Mou, style name Shaoshu, associated with Wang Anshi and Zeng Gong; his fame dominated the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mou, whose style was Shaoshu, was a companion of Wang Anshi and Zeng Gong, and his reputation stood at the forefront of his generation.

sentences.zh: 早孤，事母盡孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he served his mother with complete filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he devoted himself to his mother with the utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 誌於祿養，故屢舉進士。

translations.literal: He was intent on using salary to support her, and therefore repeatedly entered the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Determined to support her on official salary, he repeatedly sat for the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 及母病革，自誓終身不求仕。

translations.literal: When his mother's illness became critical, he vowed never to seek office for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell critically ill, he vowed never to seek office for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 客居江、淮間，士大夫敬畏之。

translations.literal: He lived as a guest between the Yangzi and Huai; scholar-officials revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived as a guest in the Yangzi and Huai regions, where scholar-officials held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 劉敞知揚州，言其孝弟忠信，足以扶世矯俗，求之朝廷，呂公著、王安石之流也。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, as prefect of Yangzhou, said his filial piety, brotherly duty, loyalty, and faithfulness were sufficient to support the age and correct custom; sought at court, he was of the caliber of Lü Gongzhu and Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang became prefect of Yangzhou, he reported that Mou's filial piety, brotherly affection, loyalty, and trustworthiness were sufficient to uphold society and correct custom, and that the court should seek out such men—men of the caliber of Lü Gongzhu and Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 詔以為揚州教授，辭。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him professor of Yangzhou; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at Yangzhou by imperial edict but declined.

sentences.zh: 敞守永興，辟入幕府，亦辭。

translations.literal: When Chang governed Yongxing, he invited him into his staff; he also declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang governed Yongxing, he invited Mou into his staff; Mou declined that as well.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，沈遘及王陶、韓維連薦之，授忠武軍推官、常州推官，皆不赴。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yingzong's reign, Shen Kui together with Wang Tao and Han Wei recommended him in succession; he was appointed push-official of the Zhongwu Army and push-official of Changzhou—all without attending.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yingzong, Shen Kui, Wang Tao, and Han Wei recommended him in succession. He was appointed push-official of the Zhongwu Army and push-official of Changzhou, but accepted neither post.

sentences.zh: 少與安石友善，安石為相，過真州與相見，侔待之如布衣交。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Anshi; when Anshi became chief councillor, passing through Zhenzhou he met with him, and Mou treated him as a plain-cloth acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had been close friends with Wang Anshi. When Anshi became chief councillor and passed through Zhen Prefecture, they met, and Mou treated him exactly as he would any ordinary friend.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 初，王回、王令、常秩與侔皆有盛名，回、令不壽，秩為隱不竟，唯侔以不仕始終。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Hui, Wang Ling, Chang Zhi, and Mou all had great fame; Hui and Ling did not live long, Zhi became a recluse without completing his path—only Mou, by not taking office, maintained this from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In those days Wang Hui, Wang Ling, Chang Zhi, and Sun Mou all enjoyed great renown. Hui and Ling died young; Zhi took up reclusion but did not see it through. Only Mou, by refusing office from first to last, held true to that path throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 劉易，忻州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi came from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 性介烈，博學好古，喜談兵。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and fierce; he was broadly learned and loved antiquity, and delighted in discussing warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and fierce by nature, widely learned and devoted to antiquity, and fond of military discourse.

sentences.zh: 韓琦知定州，上其所著《春秋論》，授太學助教、并州州學說書。

translations.literal: When Han Qi governed Dingzhou, Yi presented his authored Discourse on the Spring and Autumn Annals; he was appointed Assistant Instructor at the Imperial Academy and lecturer at the Bingzhou prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi was prefect of Dingzhou, Yi presented his Discourse on the Spring and Autumn Annals and was appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy and lecturer at the Bingzhou prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 不能屈誌仕進，寓居於虢之盧氏，習辟穀術。

translations.literal: Unable to bend his will to advance in office, he lodged in Lushi of Guo and practiced grain-avoidance techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bend his will to pursue an official career, he lodged in Lushi in Guo and practiced grain-avoidance techniques.

sentences.zh: 趙抃復薦其行誼，賜號退安處士。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian again recommended his conduct and righteousness, and he was granted the title Retired-and-Tranquil Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian recommended him again for his conduct and integrity, and the court granted him the title Retired-and-Tranquil Recluse.

sentences.zh: 易作詩，琦每為書之石，或不可其意輒滌去，琦亦再書之。

translations.literal: Yi composed poetry; Qi would inscribe it on stone for him, but if it did not suit his intent Yi would wash it away, and Qi would inscribe it again.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi wrote poetry, Han Qi would have it carved on stone; if Yi disapproved of the inscription he would wash it away, and Qi would have it carved again.

sentences.zh: 尹洙帥渭，延致尊禮，狄青代洙，遇之亦厚。

translations.literal: When Yin Zhu commanded Wei, he invited and honored him; when Di Qing replaced Zhu, he too treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhu commanded Wei, he invited Yi and treated him with honor; when Di Qing succeeded Zhu, he too treated Yi with great respect.

sentences.zh: 治平末，卒，琦作文祭之云：「剛介之性，天下能合者有幾？

translations.literal: Near the end of Zhiping he died; Qi composed a funerary text offering sacrifice, saying: "A nature so firm and upright—how many in the realm can match it?"
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhiping reign he died. Han Qi composed a funeral elegy that read, "A nature so firm and upright—how many men under Heaven can match it?"

sentences.zh: 淵源之學，古人不到者甚多。

translations.literal: " Learning of profound depth—much that the ancients did not reach."
translations.idiomatic: "Learning of such depth—much that even the ancients never attained."

sentences.zh: 」其敬之如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the respect he showed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he held him.

sentences.zh: 熙寧察訪定戶役，詔易家用處士如七品恩，得減半，示優禮雲。

translations.literal: During Xining, when household corvée was investigated and fixed, an edict granted Yi's household the favor due a seventh-rank recluse, permitting a half reduction, showing preferential courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining reign, when household corvée obligations were surveyed and fixed, an edict granted Yi's household the privileges accorded a seventh-rank recluse, allowing a fifty-percent reduction—a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 薑潛，字至之，兗州奉符人。

translations.literal: Jiang Qian, style name Zhizhi, was a native of Fengfu in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qian, whose style was Zhizhi, came from Fengfu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從孫復學《春秋》。

translations.literal: He studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Sun Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Sun Fu.

sentences.zh: 用田況舉召試學士院，為明州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: On Tian Kuang's recommendation he was summoned to examination at the Hanlin Academy and became recording adjutant of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Tian Kuang's recommendation he was summoned to the Hanlin examination and appointed recording adjutant of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以母思鄉求致仕，敕過門下，知封駁司吳奎封還之，而與韓絳共上章以薦，徙兗州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Because his mother missed her home village he sought retirement; the edict passed the Secretariat, and Wu Kui of the Sealing and Rejection Office sealed and returned it, yet together with Han Jiang submitted a memorial recommending him, and he was transferred to recording adjutant of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew homesick he petitioned to retire. The edict passed through the Secretariat, where Wu Kui of the Sealing Office returned it sealed—but Wu and Han Jiang jointly memorialized recommending him, and he was transferred to recording adjutant of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從奎辟鄆州教授，奎升堂拜其母，又薦為國子直講、韓王宮伴讀。

translations.literal: He followed Kui as professor of Yanzhou; Kui ascended the hall to bow to his mother, and again recommended him as Direct Lecturer of the Imperial Academy and companion reader in the Prince of Han's palace.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wu Kui's staff as professor at Yan Prefecture. Kui entered the hall to pay respects to Qian's mother and recommended him again as direct lecturer at the Imperial Academy and companion reader in the Prince of Han's household.

sentences.zh: 謁宗正允弼，吏引趨庭，潛不答，呼馬欲去，遂以客禮見。

translations.literal: Calling on Zongzheng Director Yunbi, an attendant led him to hurry into the courtyard; Qian did not respond, called for his horse intending to leave, and was thereupon received with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When he called on Director of the Imperial Clan Yunbi, an attendant tried to hurry him into the courtyard. Qian ignored him, called for his horse to leave, and Yunbi thereupon received him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，詔舉選人淹滯者與京官凡三十七人，潛在選中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, an edict selected thirty-seven men among stalled examination candidates and capital officials; Qian was among those chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reign an edict selected thirty-seven men from among stalled candidates and capital officials; Qian was among them.

sentences.zh: 神宗聞其賢，召對延和殿，訪以治道何以致之，對曰：「有《堯》、《舜》二《典》在，顧陛下致之之道何如。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong heard of his worth and summoned him for audience in the Yanhe Hall, asking by what means good governance might be attained; he replied: "The two Canons of Yao and Shun exist—it depends on what path Your Majesty takes to attain them."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong, hearing of his virtue, summoned him to audience in the Yanhe Hall and asked how good governance might be achieved. Qian replied, "The Canons of Yao and Shun are at hand—it depends on what path Your Majesty chooses to follow."

sentences.zh: 」知陳留縣，至數月，青苗令下，潛出錢，榜其令於縣門，已，徙之鄉落，各三日無應者。

translations.literal: " As magistrate of Chenliu County, within a few months the Green Sprouts order was issued; Qian disbursed funds and posted the order at the county gate, then moved it to villages and hamlets—after three days at each place with no respondents.
translations.idiomatic: " As magistrate of Chenliu County, within a few months the Green Sprouts order arrived. Qian disbursed the funds and posted the order at the county gate, then moved the notice to each village and hamlet. After three days at each location with no takers,

sentences.zh: 遂撤榜付吏曰：「民不願矣！

translations.literal: he thereupon removed the notice and handed it to the clerk, saying: "The people are unwilling!"
translations.idiomatic: he removed the notice and told the clerk, "The people do not wish it!"

sentences.zh: 」錢以是獨得不散。

translations.literal: " Because of this the funds alone were not distributed.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason, the funds alone were never distributed.

sentences.zh: 司農、開封疑潛沮格，各使其屬來驗，皆如令。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Agriculture and Kaifeng suspected Qian of obstruction; each sent subordinates to verify, and all found it as the order required.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Kaifeng authorities suspected Qian of obstruction and each sent subordinates to investigate; all confirmed that he had followed the regulations.

sentences.zh: 而條例司劾祥符住散青苗錢，潛知且不免，移疾去，縣人詣府請留之，不得。

translations.literal: But the Regulations Office impeached Xiangfu for halting distribution of Green Sprouts funds; Qian knew he could not escape, pleaded illness and left; county people went to the prefecture to request he be retained, without success.
translations.idiomatic: But the Regulations Office impeached Xiangfu for halting the distribution of Green Sprouts funds. Qian knew he could not escape censure, pleaded illness, and resigned. The people of the county petitioned the prefecture to keep him, but to no avail.

sentences.zh: 家居卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at home at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 連庶字居錫，安州應山人。

translations.literal: Lian Shu, style name Juxi, was a native of Yingshan in Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Shu, whose style was Juxi, came from Yingshan in An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調商水尉、壽春令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Shangshui and prefect of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Shangshui and prefect of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 興學，尊禮秀民，以勸其俗；

translations.literal: He promoted schools, honored outstanding commoners, to encourage local custom;
translations.idiomatic: He promoted schools and honored outstanding local scholars to encourage proper conduct in the district;

sentences.zh: 開瀕淮田千頃，縣大治。

translations.literal: opened a thousand qing of fields along the Huai frontier, and the county was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: reclaimed a thousand qing of fields along the Huai River, and the county flourished under his administration.

sentences.zh: 淮南王舊壘在山間，會大水，州守議取其甓為城，庶曰：「弓矢舞衣傳百世，藏於王府，非為必可用，蓋以古之物傳於今，尚有典刑也。

translations.literal: The old fort of the King of Huainan stood in the mountains; when great floods came, the prefect proposed taking its bricks for the city wall. Shu said: "Bows, arrows, and dance garments are handed down for a hundred generations, stored in the royal storehouse—not because they must be used, but because ancient things passed to the present still carry exemplary force."
translations.idiomatic: The old fort of the King of Huainan stood in the mountains. When floods came, the prefect proposed dismantling it for bricks to repair the city wall. Shu objected: "Bows, arrows, and ceremonial garments are preserved for a hundred generations in the royal treasury—not because they must be used, but because objects handed down from antiquity to the present still carry exemplary force."

sentences.zh: 」壘因是得存。

translations.literal: " The fort was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: " The fort was preserved as a result.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞監陳州稅。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested supervision of Chenzhou tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old he petitioned for the post of tax supervisor in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗送客出北門，見日西風塵，而冠蓋憧憧不已，慨然有感，即日求分司歸。

translations.literal: Once seeing a guest off through the north gate, he saw the sun setting amid wind and dust while official carriages kept streaming past without end; stirred with feeling, that very day he sought a branch-office post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while seeing a guest off through the north gate, he watched the sun set through wind and dust while official carriages streamed past without end. Deeply moved, he petitioned that very day for a branch-office appointment and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，翰林學士歐陽修、龍圖閣直學士祖無擇言庶文學行義，宜在台閣。

translations.literal: After some time, Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xiu and Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Zu Wuzhe said Shu's literary learning and conduct were fit for the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, Hanlin Academician Ouyang Xiu and Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Zu Wuzhe reported that Shu's scholarship and conduct qualified him for service at court.

sentences.zh: 以知昆山縣，辭不行。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Kunshan County but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Kunshan County but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 累遷職方員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Outer Gentleman of the Bureau of Military Appointments and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to outer gentleman of the Bureau of Military Appointments and died in office.

sentences.zh: 庶始與弟庠在鄉里，時宋郊兄弟、歐陽修皆依之。

translations.literal: Shu at first lived in the countryside with his younger brother Ku; at that time the Song Jiao brothers and Ouyang Xiu all relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and his younger brother Ku lived together in their home district, where the Song Jiao brothers and Ouyang Xiu all sought their company.

sentences.zh: 及二宋貴達，不可其志，退居二十年。

translations.literal: When the two Songs rose to eminence, unable to bend his will, he withdrew for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the two Song brothers rose to high office, Shu could not reconcile himself to their path and withdrew from public life for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 守道好修，非其人不交，非其義秋毫不可汙也。

translations.literal: He upheld the Way and loved cultivation; he would not associate with those not his kind, and would not let the slightest unrighteous matter stain him.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld the Way and loved self-cultivation; he would not associate with those he deemed unworthy, and would not let the slightest unrighteous matter stain him.

sentences.zh: 庶既死，宋郊之孫義年為應山令，緣邑人之意，作堂於法興僧舍，繪二宋及庶、庠之像祠事之。

translations.literal: After Shu died, Song Jiao's grandson Yinian became magistrate of Yingshan; following the people's wish, he built a hall at the Faxing monastery and painted portraits of the two Songs together with Shu and Ku for worship.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu died, Song Jiao's grandson Yinian became magistrate of Yingshan. At the townspeople's request he built a hall at the Faxing monastery and painted portraits of the two Song brothers together with Shu and Ku for veneration.

sentences.zh: 庠亦登科，敏於政事，號良吏，終都官郎中。

translations.literal: Ku also passed the examinations, was quick in government affairs, was called a good official, and ended as Director of the Capital Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Ku also passed the examinations, proved adept in government affairs, earned the reputation of a capable official, and ended his career as director of the Capital Bureau.

sentences.zh: 章詧字，隱之，成都雙流人。

translations.literal: Zhang Cha, style name Yinshi, was a native of Shuangliu in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cha, whose style was Yinshi, came from Shuangliu in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，鞠於兄嫂，以所事父母事之。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised by elder brother and sister-in-law, serving them with the devotion due parents.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his elder brother and sister-in-law and served them with the devotion he would have shown his parents.

sentences.zh: 博通經學，尤長《易》、《太玄》，著《發隱》三篇，明用蓍索道之法，知以數寓道之用、三摹九據始終之變。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered classical learning, especially excelling in the Book of Changes and the Supreme Mystery; he authored three scrolls of Revealing the Hidden, clarifying the method of the yarrow stalks and silk cords, knowing how numbers embody the function of the Way and how three rubbings and nine reckonings trace beginning and end in change.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics broadly and was especially adept in the Book of Changes and Yang Xiong's Supreme Mystery. He wrote three scrolls of Revealing the Hidden, elucidating the yarrow-and-cord divination method and showing how numbers embody the Way, and how three rubbings and nine reckonings trace the full cycle of change.

sentences.zh: 蜀守蔣堂、楊察、張方平、何郯、趙抃咸以逸民薦，一賜粟帛，再命州助教，不就。

translations.literal: Shu prefects Jiang Tang, Yang Cha, Zhang Fangping, He Tan, and Zhao Bian all recommended him as a recluse; once he was granted grain and silks, twice appointed prefectural assistant instructor—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu prefects Jiang Tang, Yang Cha, Zhang Fangping, He Tan, and Zhao Bian all recommended him as a recluse. He was once granted grain and silks and twice offered appointment as prefectural assistant instructor, but accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，賜號衝退處士。

translations.literal: During Jiayou he was granted the title Rush-Forward Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou reign he was granted the title Rush-Forward Recluse.

sentences.zh: 王素時為州，因更其所居之鄉曰處士，裏曰通儒，坊曰衝退。

translations.literal: Wang Su was then prefect and accordingly renamed his home township Recluse, his lane Comprehensive Scholar, and his ward Rush-Forward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was then prefect of the region and renamed Cha's home township Recluse Township, his lane Comprehensive Scholar Lane, and his ward Rush-Forward Ward.

sentences.zh: 詧由是益以道自裕，尊生養氣，憂喜、是非亦不以撓其心形。

translations.literal: Cha thereby increasingly enriched himself through the Way, honoring life and nurturing qi; joy, sorrow, right, and wrong likewise did not disturb his heart and form.
translations.idiomatic: Cha thereafter cultivated the Way with ever greater devotion, honoring life and nurturing his vital energy so that neither joy nor sorrow, neither praise nor blame, could disturb his inner peace.

sentences.zh: 嘗訪里人範百祿，謂曰：「子辟穀二十餘年，今強力尚足，子亦嘗知以氣治疾之說乎？

translations.literal: Once visiting his townsman Fan Bailu, he said: "You have avoided grain for more than twenty years, and your strength is still sufficient—have you also known the doctrine of treating illness through qi?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, visiting his neighbor Fan Bailu, he said, "You have practiced grain avoidance for more than twenty years and your strength is still ample—have you also studied the doctrine of treating illness through vital energy?"

sentences.zh: 」百祿因從扣《太玄》，詧為解述大旨，再復《摛》詞曰：「『人之所好而不足者，善也；

translations.literal: " Bailu thereupon followed to inquire about the Supreme Mystery; Cha explained the great purport, then again replied with words from Unfolding: "'What people love yet lack is goodness;"
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Bailu then pressed him on the Supreme Mystery. Cha explained its essential meaning and quoted from Unfolding: "'What people love yet lack is goodness;"

sentences.zh: 所醜而有餘者，惡也。

translations.literal: "what they detest yet have in surplus is evil."
translations.idiomatic: "what they detest yet have in surplus is evil."

sentences.zh: 君子能強其所不足，而拂其所有餘，《太玄》之道幾矣。

translations.literal: "The noble man can strengthen what he lacks and brush away what he has in surplus—the Way of the Supreme Mystery is nearly attained."
translations.idiomatic: "The noble man strengthens what he lacks and brushes away what he has in surplus—the Way of the Supreme Mystery is nearly complete."

sentences.zh: 』此子雲仁義之心，予之於《太玄》也，述斯而已。

translations.literal: "'This is Ziyun's heart of benevolence and righteousness; as for my treatment of the Supreme Mystery, I describe only this much.'"
translations.idiomatic: "'This is Yang Xiong's heart of benevolence and righteousness. As for my reading of the Supreme Mystery, I describe no more than this.'"

sentences.zh: 若苦其思，艱其言，迂溺其所以為數而忘其仁義之大，是惡足以語夫道哉？

translations.literal: "If one toils at its thought, strains at its words, becomes mired in its numerology and forgets the greatness of benevolence and righteousness—how could that suffice to speak of the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: "If one toils over its abstruse thought, strains at its difficult language, and becomes lost in numerology while forgetting the greater claims of benevolence and righteousness—how could that be enough to speak of the Way?"

sentences.zh: 」熙寧元年，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Xining he died at age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the first year of Xining, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子禩，亦好古學，嘗應行義敦遣詔。

translations.literal: His son Zhen also loved ancient learning and once responded to the edict summoning men of conduct and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen also loved ancient learning and once responded to the edict summoning men of exemplary conduct.

sentences.zh: 仍世有隱德，其所居猶存。

translations.literal: For successive generations there was hidden virtue; the place where he dwelt still remains.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family preserved its reclusive virtue, and the place where Cha lived still stands.

sentences.zh: 俞汝尚，字退翁，湖州烏程人。

translations.literal: Yu Rushang, style name Tuiweng, was a native of Wucheng in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Rushang, whose style was Tuiweng, came from Wucheng in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 少時讀書於鄣南之昆山。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at Kunshan south of Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied at Kunshan, south of Zhang.

sentences.zh: 為人溫溫有禮，議論不苟。

translations.literal: As a man he was gentle and courteous; in discussion he was never careless.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and courteous by nature, and never careless in his opinions.

sentences.zh: 不可於意，有所不言，言之未嘗妄也。

translations.literal: What did not accord with his intent he would not speak; what he spoke was never reckless.
translations.idiomatic: What did not accord with his principles he would not say; what he did say was never spoken lightly.

sentences.zh: 不肯料理生事，不以貧乏撓其懷，澹於勢利。

translations.literal: He would not trouble himself with livelihood affairs, was not disturbed in mind by poverty, and was indifferent to power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: He would not trouble himself with worldly affairs, was untroubled by poverty, and indifferent to power and profit.

sentences.zh: 聞人善言善行，記之不忘，時時為人道之。

translations.literal: Hearing others' good words and good deeds, he remembered them without forgetting and often recounted them to people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard good words or witnessed good deeds, he remembered them and often recounted them to others.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，涉曆州縣，無少營進取之心。

translations.literal: He rose through the jinshi degree and served in various prefectures and counties, with not the slightest mind to scheme for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served in various prefectures and counties, yet never showed the slightest ambition for advancement.

sentences.zh: 嘗知導江縣，新繁令卒，使者使承其乏，將資以公田，辭，不許，至則悉以周舊令之家。

translations.literal: He once governed Daojiang County; when the magistrate of Xinfan died, an envoy had him fill the vacancy and was about to supply him with public fields—he declined, was not permitted, and upon arrival gave everything to support the former magistrate's household.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as magistrate of Daojiang County. When the magistrate of Xinfan died, an envoy appointed him to fill the vacancy and offered him public fields for support. He declined but was overruled; upon taking office he gave the entire allotment to the bereaved family of his predecessor.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，簽書劍南西川判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining he was signing officer and judicial commissioner of Southwest Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining reign he served as signing officer and judicial commissioner of Southwest Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 趙抃守蜀，以簡靜為治，每旦退坐便齋，諸吏莫敢至，唯汝尚來輒排闥徑入，相對清談竟暮。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian governed Shu with simplicity and tranquility; each morning after retiring he sat in his private studio, and none of the clerks dared approach—only Rushang, when he came, would push open the door and enter directly, and they would face each other in pure conversation until evening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian governed Shu with simplicity and restraint. Each morning after court he retired to his private study, and none of his clerks dared disturb him—only Rushang would push open the door and enter unannounced, and the two would converse in leisurely talk until evening.

sentences.zh: 王安石當國，患一時故老不同己，或言汝尚清望，可置之御史，使以次彈擊。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held the state, troubled that elders of the time did not agree with him, some said Rushang's pure reputation could place him on the Censorate to impeach them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi dominated the government, troubled that veteran officials opposed his reforms, some suggested that Rushang's sterling reputation made him suitable for the Censorate, where he could be used to impeach opponents one by one.

sentences.zh: 驛召詣京師，既知所以薦用意，力辭，章再上得免。

translations.literal: He was summoned by post to the capital; once he knew the intent behind the recommendation, he strove to decline, and after submitting memorials again was excused.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital by urgent dispatch. Once he understood the purpose behind the recommendation, he declined forcefully and, after submitting further memorials, was released from the appointment.

sentences.zh: 親故有責以不能與子孫為地者，汝尚笑曰：「是乃所以為其地也。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends reproached him for failing to secure position for his descendants; Rushang smiled and said: "This is precisely how I secure their position."
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends reproached him for failing to secure official position for his descendants. Rushang smiled and said, "This is precisely how I secure their future."

sentences.zh: 」還家苦貧，未能忘祿養。

translations.literal: " Returning home in bitter poverty, he could not forget supporting himself on salary.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned home in bitter poverty, yet could not bring himself to abandon the hope of official salary.

sentences.zh: 又從趙抃於青州，遂以屯田郎中致仕。

translations.literal: He again followed Zhao Bian to Qingzhou and thereupon retired as Director of the Agricultural Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Zhao Bian to Qing Prefecture and thereafter retired with the rank of director of the agricultural colonies.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾、蘇轍、孫覺、李常皆賦詩文歎美之。

translations.literal: Su Shi, Su Zhe, Sun Jue, and Li Chang all composed poetry and prose in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi, Su Zhe, Sun Jue, and Li Chang all wrote poetry and prose in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 優遊數年，當六月徂暑，寢室不可居，出舍於門，妻黃就視之，汝尚曰：「人生七十者希，吾與夫人皆過之，可以行矣。

translations.literal: At ease for several years, when the sixth month brought full summer heat and the bedchamber was uninhabitable, he moved out to lodge by the gate; his wife Lady Huang came to see him, and Rushang said: "Few live to seventy—we have both passed that; it is time to go."
translations.idiomatic: He lived at ease for several years. In the sixth month, when the summer heat made his bedchamber unbearable, he moved outside to lodge by the gate. His wife Lady Huang came to see him, and Rushang said, "Few people live to seventy—we have both passed that mark. It is time to go."

sentences.zh: 」妻應曰：「然則我先去。

translations.literal: " His wife replied: "Then I shall go first."
translations.idiomatic: " His wife replied, "Then I shall go first."

sentences.zh: 」後三日卒。

translations.literal: " Three days later she died.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days later she died.

sentences.zh: 汝尚庀其喪，為作銘，召諸子告曰：「吾亦從此逝矣。

translations.literal: Rushang arranged her funeral, composed an inscription, summoned his sons and told them: "I too shall depart from here."
translations.idiomatic: Rushang arranged her funeral, composed an epitaph, summoned his sons, and told them, "I too shall follow her now."

sentences.zh: 」隱幾而終，相去才十日。

translations.literal: " Leaning on his armrest, he ended; only ten days separated them.
translations.idiomatic: " He died leaning on his armrest, only ten days after his wife.

sentences.zh: 孫侔，紹興中敷文閣直學士。

translations.literal: Sun Mou—in the Shaoxing era was Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mou—a different man—served as academician of the Fuwen Pavilion during the Shaoxing reign.

sentences.zh: 陽孝本，字行先，虔州贛人。

translations.literal: Yang Xiaoben, style name Xingxian, was a native of Gan in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiaoben, whose style was Xingxian, came from Gan in Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 學博行高，隱於城西通天岩。

translations.literal: His learning was broad and his conduct lofty; he lived in seclusion at Tongtian Cliff west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was broad and his conduct exemplary; he lived in seclusion at Tongtian Cliff west of the city.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌、蒲宗孟皆以山林特起薦之。

translations.literal: Su Song and Pu Zongmeng both recommended him as specially risen from mountain and forest.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song and Pu Zongmeng both recommended him as a worthy man raised from reclusion.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾自海外歸，過而愛焉，號之曰玉岩居士。

translations.literal: Su Shi, returning from overseas, passed by and came to love him, styling him Jade Cliff Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi returned from exile overseas, he visited Xiaoben and came to admire him, styling him the Jade Cliff Recluse.

sentences.zh: 嘗直造其室，知其不娶，戲以為元德秀之流。

translations.literal: Once he went straight to his dwelling, learned that he had never married, and jested that he was of the sort of Yuan Dexiu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Su Shi went straight to his dwelling, learned that he had never married, and jested that he was another Yuan Dexiu.

sentences.zh: 孝本自言為陽城之裔，故軾詩有云：「眾謂元德秀，自稱陽道州。

translations.literal: Xiaoben himself said he was a descendant of Yang Cheng; hence Shi's poem has the line: "All call him Yuan Dexiu, but he calls himself Yang of Daozhou."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoben claimed descent from Yang Cheng, which inspired Su Shi's line: "Others call him Yuan Dexiu, but he styles himself Yang of Daozhou."

sentences.zh: 」嘉之也。

translations.literal: " This was praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Shi meant this as praise.

sentences.zh: 隱遁二十年，一時名士多從之遊。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion for twenty years; famous scholars of the time often associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion for twenty years, and many celebrated scholars of the day sought his company.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，舉八行，解褐為國子錄，再轉博士。

translations.literal: During Chongning he was recommended for the Eight Conducts, left commoner's dress to become recorder of the Imperial Academy, and was transferred again to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning reign he was recommended for the Eight Conducts, entered office as recorder of the Imperial Academy, and was later promoted to erudite.

sentences.zh: 以直秘閣歸，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He returned with appointment as Direct Attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion and died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of direct attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion and died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 鄧考甫，字成之，臨川人。

translations.literal: Deng Kaofu, style name Chengzhi, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Kaofu, whose style was Chengzhi, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 第進士，曆陳留尉、萬載永明令、知上饒縣，積官奉議郎，提點開封府界河渠，坐事去官，遂閉戶著書，不復言仕。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination, served successively as magistrate of Chenliu, prefect of Yongming in Wanzai, and magistrate of Shangrao County, accumulated office to Gentleman for Discussion, supervised river works in the Kaifeng prefectural border, was dismissed for an offense, shut his doors to write books, and spoke of office no more.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Chenliu, prefect of Yongming in Wanzai, and magistrate of Shangrao County, eventually rising to gentleman for discussion and supervisor of river works on the Kaifeng prefectural border. Dismissed for an offense, he shut his doors to write and never spoke of office again.

sentences.zh: 元符末，詔求直言。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfu, an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanfu reign, an edict called for candid memorials.

sentences.zh: 考甫年八十一，上書云：「亂天下者，新法也，末流之禍，將不可勝言。

translations.literal: Kaofu at age eighty-one submitted a memorial saying: "What has thrown the realm into disorder is the New Policies; the calamities of their later currents will be beyond telling."
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-one, Kaofu submitted a memorial stating, "What has thrown the realm into disorder is the New Policies; the calamities of their later consequences will be beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 今宜以時更化，純法祖宗。

translations.literal: " Now one should transform with the times and take the ancestors as pure law."
translations.idiomatic: "The court should now reform in keeping with the times and return to the pure models of our ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」因論熙寧而下，權臣迭起，欺世誤國，曆指其事而枚數其人。

translations.literal: " He thereupon discussed from Xining downward how powerful ministers rose in succession, deceived the age and misled the state, enumerating events and counting off the men.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on to discuss how, from the Xining reign onward, powerful ministers had risen in succession, deceiving the age and misleading the state, enumerating their deeds and naming each man in turn.

sentences.zh: 蔡京嫉之，謂為詆訕宗廟，削籍羈筠州。

translations.literal: Cai Jing resented this, declared it slander of the ancestral temple, struck his name from the rolls, and detained him in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing resented the memorial, denounced it as slander of the ancestral temple, struck Kaofu from the official rolls, and exiled him to Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇寧去黨碑，釋逐臣，同類者五十三人，其五十人得歸，惟考甫與範柔中、封覺民獨否，遂卒於筠。

translations.literal: In Chongning the faction stele was removed and exiled ministers released; of fifty-three in the same category, fifty were permitted to return—only Kaofu together with Fan Rouzhong and Feng Juemin were denied, and he died in Yun.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning the faction stele was removed and exiled officials were pardoned. Of fifty-three men in the same category, fifty were allowed to return—only Kaofu, Fan Rouzhong, and Feng Juemin were excluded, and Kaofu died in Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 且死，命幼孫名世執筆，口占百餘言，其略曰：「予自謂山中宰相，虛有其才也；

translations.literal: Near death, he ordered his young grandson Mingshi to take the brush and dictated more than a hundred words; the gist ran: "I called myself a mountain chancellor, but my talent was empty;"
translations.idiomatic: Near death he had his young grandson Mingshi take dictation of more than a hundred words, which in essence read: "I called myself a mountain chancellor, but my talent was hollow;"

sentences.zh: 自謂文昌先生，虛有其詞也。

translations.literal: I called myself Master Wenchang, but my words were empty too."
translations.idiomatic: I styled myself Master Wenchang, but that too was empty talk."

sentences.zh: 不得大用於盛世，亦無憾焉，蓋有天命爾。

translations.literal: Not to be greatly employed in a flourishing age—yet I have no regret; surely there is Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Not to be greatly employed in an age of prosperity—I have no regret, for such is Heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 」所論述有《卜世大寶龜》、《伊周素蘊》、《義命雜著》、《太平策要》等，凡二百五十餘篇。

translations.literal: " His discourses included Divining the Age's Great Treasure Tortoise, Plain Substance of Yi and Zhou, Miscellaneous Writings on Righteousness and Fate, Essentials of the Great Peace, and others—more than two hundred fifty pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: " His writings included Divining the Age's Great Treasure Tortoise, Plain Substance of Yi and Zhou, Miscellaneous Writings on Righteousness and Fate, Essentials of the Great Peace, and others—more than two hundred and fifty works in all.

sentences.zh: 宇文之邵，字公南，漢州綿竹人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Zhishao, style name Gongnan, was a native of Mianzhu in Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhishao, whose style was Gongnan, came from Mianzhu in Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為文州曲水令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Qushui in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Qushui in Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉運以輕縑高其價，使縣鬻於民。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner raised the price of light silk and ordered the county to sell it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner inflated the price of light silk gauze and ordered the county to sell it to the populace.

sentences.zh: 之邵言：「縣下江上山，地狹人貧，耕者亡幾，方歲儉饑，羌夷數入寇，不可復困之以求利。

translations.literal: Zhishao said: "Below the county are rivers and uplands; the land is narrow and the people poor, with scarcely any cultivators. The year is lean and famine-stricken, and Qiang and Yi raid repeatedly—we cannot further burden them to seek profit."
translations.idiomatic: Zhishao protested: "This county lies between river and mountain—land is scarce and the people poor, with few cultivators to speak of. The year is lean and famine threatens, while Qiang and Yi raiders strike repeatedly. We cannot squeeze them further for profit."

sentences.zh: 」運使怒。

translations.literal: " The transport commissioner was angry.
translations.idiomatic: " The transport commissioner was furious.

sentences.zh: 會神宗即位求言，乃上疏曰：「天下一家也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne and sought counsel, he submitted a memorial saying: "All under Heaven is one family."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne and called for candid advice, Zhishao submitted a memorial: "All under Heaven is one family."

sentences.zh: 祖宗創業、守成之法具在。

translations.literal: The methods by which the ancestors founded and preserved the realm are fully at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The methods by which our ancestors founded and preserved the realm stand fully before us.

sentences.zh: 陛下方居諒陰，諂諛奸佞之人屏伏未動，正可念五聖之功德，常若左右前後。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just in mourning; flatterers and wicked men lie low and have not yet stirred—you should rightly keep in mind the merit and virtue of the Five Sages, as if they were at your left, right, before, and behind.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still in mourning; flatterers and schemers lie low and have not yet stirred. This is the moment to keep the merit and virtue of the Five Sages ever in mind, as though they stood at your side.

sentences.zh: 京師者，諸夏之視效，俗宜敦厚，而勿憸薄浮侈是尚。

translations.literal: The capital is what all the Xia look to for example; custom should be sincere and substantial, and not take frivolity, meanness, and extravagance as what is honored.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is what all the realm looks to for example. Its customs should be sincere and substantial, not frivolous, mean, or extravagant.

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫，民之表也，宜以名節自勵，而勢利合雜是先。

translations.literal: Grandees and ministers are the people's model; they should take fame and integrity as their spur, yet blending with power and profit comes first.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees and ministers are the people's model; they should take reputation and integrity as their standard, yet too often they chase power and profit first.

sentences.zh: 願以節義廉恥風導之，使人知自重。

translations.literal: I wish that integrity, righteousness, and sense of shame might guide them as a wind, so that people know to value themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Let integrity, righteousness, and shame guide them, so that people learn to value themselves.

sentences.zh: 千里之郡，有利未必興，有害未必除者，轉運使、提點刑獄製之也。

translations.literal: In a commandery of a thousand li, what is beneficial may not be enacted and what is harmful may not be removed—the transport commissioner and judicial intendant control this.
translations.idiomatic: In a prefecture spanning a thousand li, what is beneficial may not be enacted and what is harmful may not be removed—transport commissioners and judicial intendants hold that power.

sentences.zh: 百里之邑，有利未必興，有害未必除者，郡製之也。

translations.literal: In a district of a hundred li, what is beneficial may not be enacted and what is harmful may not be removed—the prefect controls this.
translations.idiomatic: In a county of a hundred li, the same holds true—the prefect controls what is done.

sentences.zh: 前日赦令，應在公逋負一切蠲除，而有司操之益急，督之愈甚，使上澤不下流，而細民益困。

translations.literal: The recent amnesty should have canceled all public arrears in full, yet the offices handle it ever more harshly and press ever harder, so that the sovereign's grace does not flow downward and the common people grow more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The recent amnesty should have canceled all public debts in full, yet officials enforce collection ever more harshly, so that the sovereign's grace never reaches the people and the common folk grow more desperate.

sentences.zh: 如擇賢才以為三司之官，稍假郡縣以權，則民瘼除矣。

translations.literal: If worthy talent were chosen for the Three Offices and prefectures and counties were given somewhat more authority, the people's afflictions would be removed.
translations.idiomatic: If worthy talent were placed in the Three Offices and prefectures and counties granted somewhat more authority, the people's afflictions would be relieved.

sentences.zh: 然後監番、棸、蹶、楀之盛以保安外戚，考《棠棣》、《角弓》之義以親睦九族，興墜典，拔滯淹，遠誇毗，來忠讜。

translations.literal: Then oversee the flourishing of Fan, Ju, Jue, and Yu to secure the outer kin; examine the meaning of "Appletree" and "Horn Bow" to draw the nine clans close; revive fallen rites, lift the long submerged, keep flattery far off, and welcome loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Then oversee the great clans to secure the outer kin; study the lessons of the Book of Songs to draw the nine clans close; revive fallen rites, elevate the long overlooked, keep flattery at bay, and welcome loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 凡所建置，必與大臣共議以廣其善，號令威福則專製之。

translations.literal: In all institutions established, you must deliberate with great ministers to extend what is good; commands, authority, and favor you should monopolize yourself.
translations.idiomatic: In all you establish, deliberate with your great ministers to extend what is good; reserve commands, authority, and favor to yourself alone.

sentences.zh: 如此，則天下之人思見太平可拱而俟也。」

translations.literal: Thus, the people of the realm will think of great peace as something they can await with folded arms."
translations.idiomatic: Then the people of the realm will await great peace with folded arms."

sentences.zh: 疏奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted without response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 喟然曰：「吾不可仕矣。

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "I can no longer serve in office."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "I can no longer serve in office."

sentences.zh: 」遂致仕，以太子中允歸，時年未四十。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he retired, returning as Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household while not yet forty.
translations.idiomatic: " He retired and returned home with the rank of vice director in the Crown Prince's household, not yet forty years old.

sentences.zh: 自強於學，不易其志，日與交友為經史琴酒之樂，退居十五年而終。

translations.literal: He strengthened himself in learning and did not alter his resolve, daily sharing with friends the pleasures of classics, history, zither, and wine; he withdrew for fifteen years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to learning without wavering, sharing daily with friends the pleasures of classics, history, music, and wine. He lived in retirement for fifteen years before he died.

sentences.zh: 司馬光曰：「吾聞誌不行，顧祿位如錙銖；

translations.literal: Sima Guang said: "I have heard that when one's will cannot be fulfilled, one regards salary and rank as a speck of weight;"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang said, "I have heard that when one's will cannot be fulfilled, one regards salary and rank as dust;"

sentences.zh: 道不同，視富貴如土芥。

translations.literal: "when the Way differs, one views wealth and honor as weeds."
translations.idiomatic: "when the Way differs, one views wealth and honor as weeds."

sentences.zh: 今於之邵見之矣。

translations.literal: Today I see this in Zhishao."
translations.idiomatic: Today I see this in Zhishao."

sentences.zh: 」範鎮亦曰：「之邵位下而言高，學富而行篤，少我二十一歲而先我掛冠，使吾慊然。

translations.literal: " Fan Zhen also said: "Zhishao's rank was low yet his words were lofty, his learning rich yet his conduct earnest—twenty-one years my junior yet he doffed his cap before me, which leaves me abashed."
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Zhen also said, "Zhishao held low rank yet spoke with lofty purpose; his learning was rich and his conduct earnest. Twenty-one years my junior, he retired before me—and that leaves me abashed."

sentences.zh: 」其為兩賢所推尚如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which the two worthies held him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which these two worthies held him.

sentences.zh: 吳瑛，字德仁，蘄州蘄春人。

translations.literal: Wu Ying, style name Deren, was a native of Qichun in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ying, whose style was Deren, came from Qichun in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以父龍圖閣學士遵路任補太廟齋郎，監西京竹木務，簽書淮南判官，通判池州、黃州，知郴州，至虞部員外郎。
