translations.literal: Through his father's appointment as Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Zunlu he was made Supplicant at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, supervised the Western Capital bamboo and timber office, signed as judicial commissioner of Huainan, served as vice prefect of Chizhou and Huangzhou, governed Chenzhou, and rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father Zunlu's position as Dragon Diagram Hall academician, he entered service as supplicant at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, supervised the Western Capital bamboo and timber office, served as signing judicial commissioner of Huainan, as vice prefect of Chi and Huang prefectures, and as prefect of Chen Prefecture, eventually rising to outer gentleman of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，官滿如京師，年四十六，即上書請致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping, when his term ended he went to the capital; at age forty-six he immediately submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiping, when his term ended he traveled to the capital. At forty-six he immediately petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫知之者相與出力挽留之，不聽，皆歎服以為不可及，相率賦詩飲餞於都門，遂歸。

translations.literal: Grandees and ministers who knew him joined to urge him to stay; he would not listen. All sighed in admiration that he was beyond reach, and together composed poems and held a farewell feast at the capital gate; then he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees and ministers who knew him joined in urging him to stay, but he would not listen. All sighed that he was beyond their reach, composed poems, and held a farewell feast at the capital gate before he returned home.

sentences.zh: 蘄有田，僅足自給。

translations.literal: He had fields in Qi, barely enough for self-sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He had fields in Qi, barely enough to support himself.

sentences.zh: 臨溪築室，種花釀酒，家事一付子弟。

translations.literal: By the stream he built a dwelling, planted flowers and brewed wine, and entrusted household affairs entirely to sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: He built a dwelling by the stream, planted flowers and brewed wine, and left all household affairs to his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 賓客至必飲，飲必醉，或困臥花間，客去亦不問。

translations.literal: When guests came he always drank; drinking he always became drunk; sometimes he would fall asleep among the flowers, and when guests left he did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When guests arrived he always drank, and always drank until drunk. Sometimes he fell asleep among the flowers; when guests departed he never noticed.

sentences.zh: 有臧否人物者，不酬一語，但促奴益行酒，人莫不愛其樂易而敬其高。

translations.literal: If someone praised or blamed others, he answered not a word but only urged the servant to pour more wine; none failed to love his easy cheer and revere his loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: If someone praised or condemned others in his presence, he answered not a word but urged his servant to pour more wine. Everyone loved his easy manner and revered his lofty spirit.

sentences.zh: 嘗有貴客過之，瑛酒酣而歌，以樂器扣其頭為節，客亦不以為忤。

translations.literal: Once an eminent guest visited; Ying, wine-flushed, sang and beat time on the guest's head with a musical instrument—the guest was not offended.
translations.idiomatic: Once a distinguished guest visited while Ying was deep in his cups. He sang and beat time on the guest's head with a musical instrument—the guest took no offense.

sentences.zh: 視財物如糞土，妹婿輒取家財數十萬貸人，不能償，瑛哀之曰：「 是人有母，得無重憂！

translations.literal: He viewed wealth as dung and soil; his sister's husband would take several hundred thousand of the family fortune to lend others who could not repay. Ying pitied them and said: "This man has a mother—how could he not be deeply troubled!"
translations.idiomatic: He regarded wealth as dung and soil. His sister's husband would lend out hundreds of thousands from the family fortune to borrowers who could not repay. Ying pitied them and said, "This man has a mother—how can he not be deeply troubled!"

sentences.zh: 」召而焚其券。

translations.literal: " He summoned them and burned the bonds.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned the borrowers and burned their IOUs.

sentences.zh: 門生為治田事曆歲，忽謝去，曰：「聞有言某簿書為欺者，誼不可留。

translations.literal: A student managed his fields for a year, then suddenly took leave, saying: "I hear it said that certain ledgers involve fraud—by principle I cannot remain."
translations.idiomatic: A student managed his fields for a year, then suddenly resigned, saying, "I hear that certain account books involve fraud—by principle I cannot remain."

sentences.zh: 」瑛命取前後文書示之，蓋未嘗發封也。

translations.literal: " Ying ordered the former and latter documents brought out to show him—they had never been unsealed.
translations.idiomatic: " Ying had all the documents brought out—they had never even been unsealed.

sentences.zh: 盜入室，覺而不言，且取其被，乃曰：「他物唯所欲，夜正寒，幸舍吾被。

translations.literal: A thief entered the room; Ying noticed but said nothing, and when the thief took his quilt he said: "Other things as you wish—the night is bitter cold; please leave me my quilt."
translations.idiomatic: A thief entered his room. Ying noticed but said nothing. When the thief took his quilt, he said, "Take whatever else you wish—the night is bitter cold; please leave me my quilt."

sentences.zh: 」其真率曠達類此。

translations.literal: " His genuineness, openness, and free-spiritedness were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: " His genuineness and free-spiritedness were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 哲宗朝有薦之者，召為吏部郎中，就知蘄州，皆不起。

translations.literal: During Emperor Zhezong's reign some recommended him; he was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and offered immediate governorship of Qizhou—all without accepting.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhezong he was recommended and summoned as director of the Ministry of Personnel and offered immediate appointment as prefect of Qi Prefecture—but he accepted none of these posts.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年感疾，即閉閤謝醫藥，至垂絕不亂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning he fell ill, shut his doors and refused medicine; even at the point of death he was not disordered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongning he fell ill, shut his doors, and refused medicine. Even at the point of death he remained composed.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 鬆江漁翁者，不知其姓名。

translations.literal: The Songjiang Fisherman—his name is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The Songjiang Fisherman—his name is unknown.

sentences.zh: 每棹小舟遊長橋，往來波上，扣舷飲酒，酣歌自得。

translations.literal: Each day he poled a small boat around Long Bridge, coming and going on the waves, beating the gunwale and drinking wine, singing freely in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he poled a small boat around Long Bridge, drifting on the waves, beating the gunwale as he drank and sang freely in contentment.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，閩人潘裕自京師調官回，過吳江，遇而異焉，起揖之曰：「 予視先生氣貌，固非漁釣之流，願丐緒言，以發蒙陋。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, Pan Yu of Fujian, returning from the capital on transfer, passed through Wujiang, met him and found him strange; he rose and bowed, saying: "I see in your bearing, sir, that you are surely no mere fisherman— I beg a few words to enlighten my ignorance."
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng reign, Pan Yu of Fujian, returning from the capital on a transfer assignment, passed through Wujiang and was struck by the fisherman. He rose and bowed, saying, "Your bearing, sir, is surely not that of an ordinary fisherman. I beg a few words to enlighten my ignorance."

sentences.zh: 」翁瞪視曰：「君不凡，若誠有意，能過小舟語乎？

translations.literal: " The old man stared and said: "You are no ordinary man. If you are truly sincere, can you come aboard my little boat to speak?"
translations.idiomatic: " The old man stared at him and said, "You are no ordinary man. If you are truly sincere, will you come aboard my little boat to talk?"

sentences.zh: 」裕欣然過之。

translations.literal: " Yu gladly went over.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu gladly went aboard.

sentences.zh: 翁曰：「吾厭喧煩，處閑曠，遁跡於此三十年矣。

translations.literal: The old man said: "I weary of clamor and trouble, dwell in open quiet, and have hidden my tracks here for thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: The old man said, "I weary of clamor and trouble and dwell in open quiet. I have hidden myself here for thirty years."

sentences.zh: 幼喜誦經史百家之言，後觀釋氏書，今皆棄去。

translations.literal: In youth I loved reciting the classics, histories, and the hundred schools; later I read Buddhist books—now I have cast all aside.
translations.idiomatic: In youth I loved the classics, histories, and the hundred schools; later I read Buddhist texts—now I have cast all of them aside.

sentences.zh: 唯飽食以嬉，尚何所事？

translations.literal: Only to eat my fill and amuse myself—what else is there to do?
translations.idiomatic: I eat my fill and amuse myself—what else is there to do?

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「先生澡身浴德如此。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Sir, you bathe body and virtue thus."
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "Sir, you have cultivated body and virtue to such a degree."

sentences.zh: 今聖明在上，盍出而仕乎？

translations.literal: Now a sage ruler sits above—why not emerge and take office?"
translations.idiomatic: A sage emperor reigns above—why not emerge and serve?"

sentences.zh: 」笑曰：「君子之道，或出或處，吾雖不能棲隱岩穴，追園、綺之蹤，竊慕老氏曲全之義。

translations.literal: " He laughed and said: "The noble man's Way may lead out or lead in. Though I cannot dwell hidden in cliff caves and follow the tracks of Master Yuan and Master Qi, I privately admire Laozi's doctrine of bending to preserve wholeness."
translations.idiomatic: " He laughed and said, "The noble man's Way may lead outward or inward. Though I cannot dwell in mountain caves and follow the tracks of the recluses of the Qin, I privately admire Laozi's teaching of bending to preserve wholeness."

sentences.zh: 且養誌者忘形，養形者忘利，致道者忘心，心形俱忘，其視軒冕如糞土耳，與子出處異趣，子勉之。

translations.literal: Moreover, he who nurtures will forget form; he who nurtures form forgets profit; he who attains the Way forgets mind—when mind and form are both forgotten, he views carriage and cap as dung and soil. Your path of in and out differs from mine—press on."
translations.idiomatic: He who nurtures the will forgets the body; he who nurtures the body forgets profit; he who attains the Way forgets the mind. When mind and body are both forgotten, carriage and cap are dung and soil. Your path differs from mine—press on with yours."

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「 裕也不才，幸聞先生之高義，敢問舍所在。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "I am without talent, but fortunate to hear your lofty righteousness—may I ask where your dwelling lies?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "I am without talent, but fortunate to hear your lofty conduct—may I ask where your dwelling lies?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾姓名且不欲人知，況居室耶！

translations.literal: " He said: "I do not wish people to know even my name—how much less my dwelling!"
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I do not wish people to know even my name—how much less where I live!"

sentences.zh: 」飲畢，長揖使裕反其所，鼓枻而去。

translations.literal: " When the drinking was done, he bowed deeply and sent Yu back to his place, then beat the oars and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " When they had finished drinking, he bowed deeply, sent Yu back to shore, and poled his boat away.

sentences.zh: 杜生者，潁昌人。

translations.literal: Du Sheng was a man of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Sheng came from Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 不知其名，縣人呼為杜五郎。

translations.literal: His name is unknown; people of the county call him Du the Fifth.
translations.idiomatic: His name is unknown; locals called him Du the Fifth.

sentences.zh: 所居去縣三十里，有屋兩間，與其子並居，前有空地丈餘，即為籬門，生不出門者三十年。

translations.literal: His dwelling lay thirty li from the county seat; he had two rooms and lived together with his son. Before the house was open ground of more than a zhang, which served as his hedge gate. He had not gone out for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived thirty li from the county seat in two rooms shared with his son. A strip of open ground more than a zhang wide before the house served as his hedge gate. He had not left home for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 黎陽尉孫軫往訪之。

translations.literal: Sun Zhen, magistrate of Liyang, went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen, magistrate of Liyang, went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 其人頗灑落，自陳村人無所能，官人何為見顧。

translations.literal: The man was quite free and easy, declaring himself a villager without ability—why should an official trouble to visit?
translations.idiomatic: The man was quite at ease, saying he was only a villager without ability—why should an official trouble to visit?

sentences.zh: 軫問所以不出門之因，笑曰：「以告者過也。

translations.literal: Zhen asked the reason he did not go out; he laughed and said: "Those who told you exaggerated."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked why he never went out. He laughed and said, "Those who told you exaggerated."

sentences.zh: 」指門外一桑曰：「憶十五年前，亦曾納涼其下，何謂不出？

translations.literal: " He pointed to a mulberry outside the gate and said: "I recall that fifteen years ago I also took shade beneath it—what do you mean, not going out?"
translations.idiomatic: " He pointed to a mulberry outside and said, "Fifteen years ago I took shade beneath it—what do you mean, never going out?"

sentences.zh: 但無用於時，無求於人，偶自不出耳，何足尚哉。

translations.literal: I am simply of no use to the age and ask nothing of others—I happen not to go out, that's all. What is there to admire?
translations.idiomatic: I am simply of no use to the age and ask nothing of others—I happen not to go out. What is there to admire?

sentences.zh: 」問所以為生，曰：「昔時居邑之南，有田五十畝，與某兄同耕。

translations.literal: " Asked how he made a living, he said: "Formerly I lived south of the town and had fifty mu of fields, which I farmed together with a certain elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: " Asked how he made a living, he said, "Formerly I lived south of the town with fifty mu of fields, which I farmed together with my elder brother."

sentences.zh: 迨兄子娶婦，度所耕不足贍，乃盡以與兄，而攜妻子至此，蒙鄉人借屋，遂居之。

translations.literal: When my brother's son married, I judged that what we farmed would not suffice to support them, so I gave it all to my brother and brought wife and children here; townspeople lent us a house, and we settled.
translations.idiomatic: When my brother's son married, I saw that our fields could not support them all, so I gave everything to my brother and brought my wife and children here. Neighbors lent us this house, and we settled.

sentences.zh: 唯與人擇日，又賣醫藥以給飦粥，亦有時不繼。

translations.literal: I only chose auspicious days for others and sold medicines to supply gruel—sometimes we still went without.
translations.idiomatic: I chose auspicious days for others and sold medicines to buy gruel—sometimes we still went without.

sentences.zh: 後子能耕，荷長者見憐，與田三十畝使之耕，尚有餘力，又為人傭耕，自此食足。

translations.literal: Later my son could farm; an elder took pity and gave him thirty mu to cultivate. He still had strength left and hired out as a farm laborer—since then food has been sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Later my son learned to farm. A local elder took pity and gave him thirty mu. With strength to spare he also hired out as a laborer—since then we have had enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 鄉人貧，以醫術自業者多。

translations.literal: Townsmen are poor; many make medicine their trade.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople are poor; many make a living from medicine.

sentences.zh: 念己食既足，不當更兼他利，由是擇日賣藥，一切不為。

translations.literal: Reflecting that my food was already sufficient, I ought not to take other profit as well—therefore I chose days and sold medicine no more, and do nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Since we had enough to eat, I should not take other profit as well. I stopped choosing days and selling medicine, and do nothing else.

sentences.zh: 」問常日何所為，曰：「端坐耳。

translations.literal: " Asked what he did on ordinary days, he said: "Just sit upright."
translations.idiomatic: " Asked what he did on ordinary days, he said, "Just sit upright."

sentences.zh: 」「頗觀書否？

translations.literal: " "Do you read books much?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Do you read much?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「二十年前，曾有人遺一書策，無題號，其間多說浮名經，當時極愛其議論，今忘之，並書亦不知所在矣。

translations.literal: " He said: "Twenty years ago someone left me a book without a title; it spoke much of the Floating Name Classic. I greatly loved its arguments then—now I have forgotten, and do not know where the book is either."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "Twenty years ago someone left me a book without a title, much of it about the Floating Name Classic. I loved its arguments then—now I have forgotten them, and the book itself is lost."

sentences.zh: 」時盛寒，布袍草屩，室中枵然，而氣韻閑曠，言詞精簡，蓋有道之士也。

translations.literal: " It was bitter cold; he wore cloth robe and straw sandals, the room was bare—yet his bearing was leisurely and open, his words concise and refined; he was surely a man of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: " It was bitter cold. He wore a cloth robe and straw sandals in a bare room—yet his bearing was serene and his words concise and refined. He was surely a man of the Way.

sentences.zh: 問其子之為人，曰：「村童也，然性質甚淳厚，不妄言，不敢嬉。

translations.literal: Asked about his son's character, he said: "A village lad, but his nature is very sincere—he does not speak rashly and dares not play idly."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about his son, he said, "A village lad, but very sincere—he does not speak rashly and dares not idle about."

sentences.zh: 唯間一至縣買鹽酪，可數行跡以待其歸，徑往徑還，未嘗旁遊一步也。

translations.literal: Only occasionally he goes once to the county to buy salt and dairy—you can count his footprints waiting for his return; he goes straight there and straight back, never wandering a single step aside.
translations.idiomatic: Only occasionally he goes to the county for salt and dairy. You can count his footprints waiting for his return—he goes straight there and straight back, never wandering aside.

sentences.zh: 」軫嗟歎，留連久之，乃去。

translations.literal: " Zhen sighed in admiration, lingered long, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen sighed in admiration, lingered a long while, and departed.

sentences.zh: 後至延安幕府，為沈括言之。

translations.literal: Later, at the Yan'an staff headquarters, he told Shen Kuo of this.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the Yan'an military headquarters, he told Shen Kuo the story.

sentences.zh: 括時理軍書，迨夜半，疲極未臥，聞軫談及此，及頓忘其勞。

translations.literal: Kuo was then handling military documents; nearing midnight, utterly weary and not yet abed, he heard Zhen speak of this and instantly forgot his fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kuo was handling military documents. Near midnight, utterly weary and still not abed, he heard Zhen's account and instantly forgot his fatigue.

sentences.zh: 順昌山人。

translations.literal: The Shunchang Mountain Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunchang Mountain Man.

sentences.zh: 靖康末，有避亂於順昌山中者，深入得茅舍，主人風裁甚整，即之語，士君子也。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingkang, some fleeing turmoil in the Shunchang mountains went deep within and found a thatched hut; the master's bearing was very proper—approaching to speak, he was a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingkang reign, refugees fleeing turmoil in the Shunchang mountains found a thatched hut deep in the hills. The master's bearing was dignified; on speaking with him, they found a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 怪而問曰：「諸君何事挈妻孥能至是耶？

translations.literal: Wondering, they asked: "Why is it, gentlemen, that you can bring wives and children to such a place?"
translations.idiomatic: Astonished, they asked, "How is it that you gentlemen can bring wives and children to such a remote place?"

sentences.zh: 」因語之故。

translations.literal: " They thereupon told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " They told him their story.

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「亂何自而起耶？

translations.literal: The master said: "From what did the turmoil arise?"
translations.idiomatic: The master asked, "From what did this turmoil arise?"

sentences.zh: 」眾爭為言，主人嗟惻久之，曰：「我父為仁宗朝人也，自嘉祐末卜居於此，因不復出。

translations.literal: " The crowd vied to explain; the master sighed in compassion for a long while and said: "My father was a man of Emperor Renzong's reign. From the end of Jiayou we divined a dwelling here and have not gone out since."
translations.idiomatic: " They all spoke at once. The master sighed compassionately for a long while and said, "My father lived in the reign of Emperor Renzong. We settled here at the end of Jiayou and have not gone out since."

sentences.zh: 以我所聞，但知有熙寧紀年，亦不知於今幾何年矣。」

translations.literal: As far as I have heard, I only know there is the Xining reign era—I do not know how many years it has been to the present."
translations.idiomatic: As far as I know, there is only the Xining reign era—I have no idea how many years have passed since then."

sentences.zh: 南安翁者。

translations.literal: The Nan'an Old Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Nan'an Old Man.

sentences.zh: 漳州陳元忠客居南海日，嘗赴省試過南安，會日暮，投宿野人家，茅茨數椽，竹樹茂密可愛。

translations.literal: When Chen Yuanzhong of Zhangzhou was a guest in the Southern Sea, he once went to the provincial examination and passed through Nan'an; as evening came he lodged at a rustic home—several thatched rafters, bamboo and trees dense and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yuanzhong of Zhangzhou was living in the south, he once traveled to the provincial examination and passed through Nan'an. At dusk he lodged at a rustic home—a few thatched rooms amid dense, lovely bamboo and trees.

sentences.zh: 主翁雖麻衣草屨，而舉止談對宛若士人。

translations.literal: Though the host wore hemp robe and straw sandals, his bearing and conversation were like a gentleman's.
translations.idiomatic: Though the host wore hemp robe and straw sandals, his bearing and conversation were those of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 几案間有文籍散亂，視之皆經、子也。

translations.literal: On the table lay books scattered in disorder; looking at them, they were all classics and masters.
translations.idiomatic: Books lay scattered on the table—all classics and masters.

sentences.zh: 陳叩之曰：「翁訓子讀書乎？

translations.literal: Chen inquired: "Sir, do you instruct your son in reading?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen asked, "Sir, do you teach your son to read?"

sentences.zh: 」 曰：「種園為生耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "We make a living from gardening, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "We make our living from gardening, that's all."

sentences.zh: 」「亦入城市乎？

translations.literal: " "Do you also go into the city?"
translations.idiomatic: " "Do you also go into town?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「十五年不出矣。

translations.literal: " He said: "I have not gone out for fifteen years."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I have not gone into town for fifteen years."

sentences.zh: 」 問：「藏書何用？

translations.literal: " Chen asked: "What use are the books?"
translations.idiomatic: " Chen asked, "What are the books for?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「偶有之耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "I happen to have a few, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I happen to have a few, that's all."

sentences.zh: 」因雜以他語。

translations.literal: " He then mixed in other topics of talk.
translations.idiomatic: " He then turned the conversation to other matters.

sentences.zh: 少焉，風雨暴作，其二子歸，舍鉏揖客，人物不類農家子。

translations.literal: Before long wind and rain burst forth; his two sons returned, set down their hoes and bowed to the guest—their bearing was not like farmers' sons.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a storm broke. His two sons returned, set down their hoes, and bowed to the guest—their bearing was nothing like that of farm boys.

sentences.zh: 翁進豆羹享客，不復共談，遲明別去。

translations.literal: The old man brought bean soup to entertain the guest and spoke no more together; at dawn Chen took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: The old man served bean soup and spoke no further with him. At dawn Chen departed.

sentences.zh: 陳以事留城中，翌日，見翁倉遑而行，陳追詰之曰：「翁雲十五年不出城，何為到此？

translations.literal: Chen was detained in town on business; the next day he saw the old man hurrying along in distress. Chen pursued and questioned him: "You said you had not gone into the city for fifteen years—why have you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen was detained in town on business. The next day he saw the old man hurrying along in distress. Chen caught up with him and asked, "You said you had not entered the city for fifteen years—why are you here?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾以急事不容不出。

translations.literal: " He said: "An urgent matter would not permit me to stay in."
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "An urgent matter left me no choice but to come out."

sentences.zh: 」問之，乃大兒於關外鬻果失稅，為關吏所拘。

translations.literal: " On inquiry, it turned out his elder son, selling fruit outside the pass, had failed to pay tax and was detained by the pass officer.
translations.idiomatic: " On inquiry he learned that his elder son, selling fruit outside the pass, had failed to pay tax and been detained by the pass officer.

sentences.zh: 陳為謁監征，至則已捕送郡。

translations.literal: Chen interceded with the tax supervisor, but upon arrival the son had already been seized and sent to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen interceded with the tax supervisor, but by the time he arrived the son had already been sent to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 翁與小兒偕詣庭下，長子當杖，翁懇白郡守曰：「某老鈍無能，全藉此子贍給。

translations.literal: The old man went with his younger son to the court; the elder son was to receive the staff. The old man pleaded to the prefect: "I am old, dull, and without ability—all my support depends on this son."
translations.idiomatic: The old man went with his younger son to the yamen. The elder son was to be beaten. The old man pleaded with the prefect, "I am old and useless—all our support depends on this son."

sentences.zh: 若渠不勝杖，則翌日乏食矣。

translations.literal: If he cannot bear the staff, we will lack food tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot bear the beating, we will have no food tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 願以身代之。

translations.literal: I wish to take the punishment in his place."
translations.idiomatic: Let me take the punishment in his place."

sentences.zh: 」小兒曰：「大人豈可受杖，某願代兄。

translations.literal: " The younger son said: "How can Father receive the staff? I wish to take my brother's place."
translations.idiomatic: " The younger son said, "Father cannot be beaten—I will take my brother's place."

sentences.zh: 」大兒又以罪在己，甘心焉，三人爭不決。

translations.literal: " The elder son, since the fault was his own, was willing in heart; the three disputed without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: " The elder son, knowing the fault was his, accepted it willingly. The three argued without reaching agreement.

sentences.zh: 小兒來父耳旁語，若將有所請，翁叱之，兒必欲前。

translations.literal: The younger son came to whisper at his father's ear as if to make some request; the old man scolded him, but the boy insisted on pressing forward.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son whispered at his father's ear as though to make a request. The old man scolded him, but the boy pressed forward anyway.

sentences.zh: 郡守疑之，呼問所以，對曰：「大人元係帶職正郎，宣和間累典州郡。

translations.literal: The prefect grew suspicious and summoned him to ask the reason; he replied: "Father was originally a ranked Right Gentleman with concurrent appointment, and during Xuanhe repeatedly governed prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect grew suspicious and summoned the boy to ask why. He replied, "Father was originally a ranked right gentleman with concurrent appointment, and during the Xuanhe reign repeatedly governed prefectures."

sentences.zh: 」翁急拽其衣使退，曰：「兒狂，妄言。

translations.literal: " The old man hastily pulled his robe to make him withdraw, saying: "The boy is mad—he speaks rashly."
translations.idiomatic: " The old man hastily pulled him back, saying, "The boy is mad—he speaks nonsense."

sentences.zh: 」守詢誥敕在否，兒曰：「見作一束置甕中，埋於山下。

translations.literal: " The prefect asked whether the patent edicts still existed; the boy said: "They are bundled in a jar and buried beneath the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: " The prefect asked whether the patent edicts still existed. The boy said, "They are bundled in a jar buried beneath the mountain."

sentences.zh: 」守立遣吏隨兒發取，果得之，即延翁上坐，謝而釋其子。

translations.literal: " The prefect immediately sent an official with the boy to dig them up; they were indeed found. He thereupon invited the old man to the seat of honor, apologized, and released his son.
translations.idiomatic: " The prefect immediately sent an official with the boy to dig them up—and found them. He invited the old man to the seat of honor, apologized, and released his son.

sentences.zh: 次日，枉駕訪之，室已虛矣。

translations.literal: " The next day he went in person to visit; the dwelling was already empty.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he went in person to visit, but the dwelling was already empty.

sentences.zh: 張舉字子厚，常州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ju, style name Zihou, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju, whose style was Zihou, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士甲科。

translations.literal: He placed in the top class of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top class.

sentences.zh: 以無他兄弟，獨養其親，不忍斯須去左右。

translations.literal: Having no other brothers, he alone supported his parents and could not bear to leave their side even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Having no other brothers, he alone supported his parents and could not bear to leave their side even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 親友強之仕，乃調青溪主簿，亦不之官。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends urged him to take office; he was assigned registrar of Qingxi but did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends urged him to serve. He was assigned registrar of Qingxi but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 閉戶讀書四十年，手校數萬卷，無一字舛。

translations.literal: He shut his doors to read for forty years, collating tens of thousands of scrolls by hand without a single erroneous character.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself in to read for forty years, collating tens of thousands of scrolls by hand without a single erroneous character.

sentences.zh: 窮經著書，至夜分不寐。

translations.literal: He exhaustively studied the classics and wrote books, not sleeping until the middle of the night.
translations.idiomatic: He exhaustively studied the classics and wrote books, often not sleeping until midnight.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，近臣薦其高行。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, close ministers recommended his lofty conduct.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng reign, court intimates recommended his exemplary conduct.

sentences.zh: 至於元祐，大臣復薦之，起教授潁州，辭不就。

translations.literal: By Yuanyou, great ministers recommended him again; he was summoned as professor of Yingzhou but declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanyou reign great ministers recommended him again. He was summoned as professor at Ying Prefecture but declined.

sentences.zh: 於是孫覺、胡宗愈、范祖禹交章言曰：「舉且死草萊，後世必以為朝廷失士。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sun Jue, Hu Zongyu, and Fan Zuyu submitted successive memorials saying: "Ju is about to die in the fields—later ages will surely judge that the court has lost a scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Sun Jue, Hu Zongyu, and Fan Zuyu submitted successive memorials saying, "Ju is about to die in obscurity—posterity will surely judge that the court has lost a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 」蘇軾言之尤切。

translations.literal: " Su Shi spoke on the matter with especial urgency.
translations.idiomatic: " Su Shi spoke on the matter with especial urgency.

sentences.zh: 詔拜秘書省校書郎，敕郡縣致禮敦遣，竟不出。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him collator of the Secretariat; the command ordered prefectures and counties to extend ritual courtesy and urge him onward—he never emerged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him collator in the Secretariat and ordered prefectures and counties to extend ceremonial courtesy and urge him to serve—he never emerged.

sentences.zh: 舉孝弟修於家，忠信行於友，聲名聞於人，蹈中守常，從容不迫，為當時名流所慕，以不造門為恥。

translations.literal: Ju cultivated filial piety and brotherly duty at home, loyalty and faith among friends; his fame was heard among men. He trod the mean and upheld constancy, easy and unhurried; the celebrated men of the age admired him, and regarded not visiting his door as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ju cultivated filial piety and brotherly affection at home and loyalty and trustworthiness among friends; his reputation spread widely. He held to the golden mean with calm unhurried grace. The celebrated men of his age admired him, and regarded failure to visit his door as a mark of shame.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Chongning.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔以舉隱德丘園，聲聞顯著，賜諡曰正素先生。

translations.literal: The following year, an edict cited Ju's hidden virtue in garden and grove, his fame conspicuously heard, and granted the posthumous title Master Upright-and-Plain.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict cited his hidden virtue in retirement and his conspicuous reputation, and granted the posthumous title Master Upright-and-Plain.
